rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is heartfelt praise of a living, rational being's beautiful qualities or benefactions, with love and reverence.
rows.anchor: الثناء على الجميل من النعمة أو غيرها مع المحبة والإجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is broader than hamd: it may precede a good deed and may describe an inanimate object, while hamd requires actual merit and follows benefaction.
rows.anchor: قد ثبت أن المدح أعم من الحمد

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns against excessive flatterers, supporting the distinction between unearned praise and merited hamd.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:"احثوا التراب في وجه المداحين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever fails to thank people has not thanked God.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:"من لم يحمد الناس لم يحمد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is preferable to madḥ and shukr because it covers both God's intrinsic qualities and His benefactions, whereas shukr applies only to favors and madḥ need not reflect real merit.
rows.anchor: الحمد أعمهما لأنك تحمد الإنسان على صفاته الذاتية وعلى عطائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording الحمد لله states that God merits praise for His qualities and deeds, whereas أحمد الله reports only the speaker's own act of praising.
rows.anchor: في حين أن عبارة "الحمد لله" لا تختص بفاعل معين فهو المحمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike a first-person verb, الحمد لله is not limited to a speaker or to the finite time in which that person can praise; its praise is unceasing.
rows.anchor: الحمد فيها مستمر غير منقطع

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says أحمد الله declares the speaker able to praise, while الحمد لله says God was praised before any created praiser and remains praised eternally.
rows.anchor: جاء في تفسير الرازي أنه لو قال " احمد الله " أفاد ذلك كون القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal الحمد لله conveys stable, lasting praise, unlike the verbal sentence أحمد الله, which suggests occurrence and renewal.
rows.anchor: الجملة الاسمية دالة على الثبوت وهي أقوى وأدوم من الجملة الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحمد لله also declares praise to be God's rightful property because of His abundant favors; a personal act of praising does not assert this entitlement.
rows.anchor: الحمد والثناء حق لله وملكه فانه تعالى هو المستحق للحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hamd is a state of the heart, someone saying أحمد الله without reverence may lie, whereas الحمد لله remains true whether or not the speaker is attentive.
rows.anchor: والحمد: عبارة عن صفة القلب وهي اعتقاد كون ذلك المحمود متفضلا منعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this to لا إله إلا الله, which does not claim a personal act of witnessing; a hypocrite can lie by saying أشهد, as 63:1 states.
rows.anchor: والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading الحمدُ لله makes a stable nominal sentence; the accusative requires an implied verb and yields a verbal sentence or command, so the nominative is stronger.
rows.anchor: قراءة الرفع تدل على أن الجملة اسمية في حين أن قراءة النصب تدل على أن الجملة فعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the accusative is construed as a command to praise, a command does not establish that its object deserves praise; the declarative nominative is preferable.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالشيء لا يعني أن المأمور به مستحق للفعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the definite article in الحمد as referring to the known praise among its hearers.
rows.anchor: قد تكون لتعريف العهد فيكون المعنى: أن الحمد المعروف بينكم هو لله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others take the article as generic and exhaustive, covering every kind and instance of praise.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون لتعريف الجنس على سبيل الاستغراق فيدل على استغراق الأحمدة كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the exhaustive sense, supported by the Prophetic prayer اللهم لك الحمد كله: all known praise belongs to God without exception.
rows.anchor: "اللهم لك الحمد كله" فدل على استغراق الحمد كله

rows.speaker: أكثر النحاة والمفسرين
rows.claim: Most grammarians and exegetes treat الحمد لله as a report that praise belongs to God.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر النحاة والمفسرين: أن الحمد لله إخبار

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: Another group treats the expression as performative because it embodies love.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال: أنها إنشاء لأن فيها استشعار المحبة

rows.speaker: قسم
rows.claim: A further view classifies it as a report that also contains a performative act.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال: أنها خبر يتضمن إنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can function as either report or invocation depending on context, letting the speaker affirm God's praise while expressing appreciation and reverence.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله هي من العبارات التي يمكن أن تستعمل خبرا وإنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحمد لله can carry both report and invocation, but إن الحمد لله forces a performative reading and loses that breadth.
rows.anchor: عندما تدخل عليه " إن " لا يمكن إلا أن يكون إنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic particles can shift a phrase between invocation and report, as رحمه الله and رزقك الله differ from their versions introduced by قد.
rows.anchor: من المعلوم انه في اللغة قد تدخل بعض الأدوات على عبارات فتغير معناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting لله in لله الحمد normally marks restriction, but al-Fatiha's context is not one of exclusive praise: worldly praise can also be directed to people, unlike exclusive worship.
rows.anchor: الحمد في الدنيا قد تقال لأستاذ أو سلطان عادل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context contrast explains the order: al-Fatiha has believers confessing worship and asking for help, while al-Jathiya answers unbelievers' claims about life and death by foregrounding God's praise.
rows.anchor: أما في سورة الجاثية فالمقام في الكافرين وعقائدهم وقد نسبوا الحياة والموت لغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jathiya repeatedly discusses God's lordship over the heavens, earth, creation, and worlds; its closing praise gathers these themes, unlike al-Fatiha's focus on the worlds and their accountable groups.
rows.anchor: جمع الربوبية في السموات والأرض والعالمين في آية واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jathiya's mention of divine majesty in heaven and earth answers the arrogant rejecters described in 45:7–9; al-Fatiha has no corresponding context of arrogance.
rows.anchor: دل على مظهر من مظاهر الاستكبار لذا ناسب أن يرد ذكر الكبرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using God's proper name means He deserves praise for His essence, not merely for one attribute such as power or creation.
rows.anchor: عند ذكر الذات (الله) فإنها تعني انه سبحانه يستحق الحمد لذاته لا لوصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Allah suits the move to worship because it denotes the deity to be worshipped, and the author says it is paired with worship more than fifty times in the Quran.
rows.anchor: لفظ الجلالة (الله) يعنى الإله المعبود مأخوذة من أله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb al-alamin is the apt continuation after praise: Rabb means owner, master, educator, benefactor, and caretaker, and encompasses God's attributes.
rows.anchor: الرب هو المالك والسيد والمربي والمنعم والقيِّم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-alamin is suited to accountable and rational beings, unlike awalim, which can name classes of animals, insects, or inanimate things.
rows.anchor: اختيار العالمين على العوالم أمر بلاغي يعني ذلك أن العالمين خاص للمكلفين وأولي العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-alamin may refer to all accountable generations or a subset, as in Lot's people; it fits al-Fatiha's concern with guidance and human moral groups and answers Jews who claimed God only as their Lord.
rows.anchor: جاءت رب العالمين لتشمل كل العالمين لا بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb also fits the request for guidance because education is a core sense of lordship and guidance frequently follows the name Rabb in scripture.
rows.anchor: من معاني الرب المربي وهي أشهر معانيه وأولى مهام الرب الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic morphology, fa'lan (as in Rahman) suggests fullness and a renewed, occurring state, while fa'il (Rahim) suggests a stable quality; examples include غضبان/عطشان and طويل/ضعيف.
rows.anchor: الصفة فعلان تمثل الحدوث والتجدد والامتلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining Rahman and Rahim presents mercy as both renewed and permanently established, preventing either name alone from suggesting that mercy may lapse.
rows.anchor: جاء سبحانه بالصفتين مجتمعتين ليدل على أن صفاته الثابتة والمتجددة هي الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman comes first to stress immediate, renewed, abundant mercy for people who favor what arrives soon, as 75:20 observes.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنسان في طبيعته عجول وكثيراً ما يؤثر الإنسان الشيء الآتي السريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahim after Rabb signals that mercy should mark a true educator, master, and caretaker; God also described His Messenger as merciful.
rows.anchor: ووقوع كلمة " الرحيم " بعد كلمة الرب يدلنا على أن الرحمة هي من صفات الله تعالى العليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither of the two mass-transmitted readings Malik and Malik is superior; together they convey both ownership and kingship.
rows.anchor: ليس هناك قراءة أولى من قراءة فكلتا القراءتين متواترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner may personally manage a possession and provide for its dependents, while the king exercises broader rule and public administration; God is both.
rows.anchor: المالك يتصرف في ملكه كما لا يتصرف الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of the worlds already covers worldly life; يوم الدين includes the working days that precede judgment, so adding الدنيا is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: مالك يوم الدين هو مالك يوم الجزاء يعني ملك ما قبله من أيام العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Din is preferable to qiyama because it means recompense and includes judgment, reckoning, obedience, and subjugation, all concerning accountable beings.
rows.anchor: الدين بمعنى الجزاء وهو يشمل جميع أنواع القيامة من أولها إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God owner of the day itself comprehensively includes everyone, everything, and every event within it.
rows.anchor: مالك اليوم هو ملك لكل ما فيه وكل من فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence praises God for His essence, lordship, properly placed mercy, and ownership and kingship on the day of recompense.
rows.anchor: محمود في رحمته يضعها حيث يجب أن توضع وهو محمود يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening attributes span all time: praise before creation, at creation, through continuing mercy, and through the unending recompense of the afterlife, as 28:70 says.
rows.anchor: استغرق الحمد كل الأزمنة من الأزل إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting إياك restricts worship and reliance to God alone; the author compares this exclusive order with exclusive trust and turning in 60:4 and 14:12.
rows.anchor: قدم المفعولين لنعبد ونستعين وهذا التقديم للاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 67:29 faith is not exclusive to God, since believers also affirm messengers, books, angels, the Last Day, and destiny; reliance, by contrast, is exclusively on God.
rows.anchor: الإيمان ليس محصورا بالله وحده فقط بل علينا الإيمان بالله ورسله وكتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating إياك explicitly restricts both worship and reliance independently; one pronoun could leave reliance unexpressed or imply that either depends on the other.
rows.anchor: وجب التكرار في الضمير إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance is left unrestricted so it includes every matter for which a person may seek God's help, rather than one worldly task.
rows.anchor: أطلق سبحانه فعل الاستعانة ولم يحدد نستعين على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural نعبد ونستعين emphasizes communal life: congregational prayer, pilgrimage, charity, jihad, festivals, fasting, and believers' shared brotherhood; it includes the speaker among them.
rows.anchor: في هذا إشارة إلى أهمية الجماعة في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is possible only with God's aid and enabling; asking for help cures pride and admits human weakness and inability to bear the trust unaided.
rows.anchor: الإنسان لا يستطيع أن يقوم بعبادة الله إلا بإعانة الله له وتوفيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship precedes reliance because worship is the purpose of creating humans and jinn (51:56), while reliance is a means to worship; God's right also precedes a request.
rows.anchor: العبادة هي علة خلق الإنس والجن (وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون) (الذاريات 56)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person praise to direct address is iltifat; it renews attention and suits addressing God as present when worshippers pray.
rows.anchor: في البلاغة يسمى هذا الانتقال من الغائب للمخاطب أو المتكلم أو العكس " الإلتفات "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligatory repeated request for guidance shows its importance: people cannot find the straight path unaided, and prayer requires reciting al-Fatiha; this differs from the sunnah supplication in 2:201.
rows.anchor: لا صلاة بدون فاتحة فلذا يجب الدعاء به في الصلاة الفريضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance means inspiration and direction, and هدى may govern its object directly, with إلى, or with ل, as the cited verses demonstrate.
rows.anchor: والهداية: هي الإلهام والدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes constructions by stages: إلى can bring an outsider to the path; direct transitivity can describe someone on or off it; ل marks reaching the goal after traveling it.
rows.anchor: إذا وصل ويحتاج من يعرفه بالطريق وأحواله نستعمل الفعل المتعدي بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples contrast the stages: Abraham's father and hypocrites need direction to the path, while the prophets and the Messenger are already on it; إلى likewise marks an outsider in 38:22 and 10:35.
rows.anchor: واستعملت لمن هم في الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says ل is never used with sirat or sabil because these are means rather than destinations; it marks final guidance and is used with God or the Quran.
rows.anchor: الهداية مع اللام لم تستعمل مع السبيل أو الصراط أبدا في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 10:35 God's guidance to the truth reaches its final destination, unlike the false gods' inability to bring people there.
rows.anchor: الله وحده يرشدك ويوصلك إلى خاتمة الهدايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 5:16 direct transitivity suits people who already follow God's favor, while إلى suits those in darkness who need to be brought to the path.
rows.anchor: والذي في الظلمات هو بعيد عن الصراط ويحتاج إلى من يوصله إلى الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct object in اهدنا الصراط combines the stages: ask God both to bring the straying to the path and to show and steady those already on it.
rows.anchor: لجمع عدة معاني فالذي انحرف عن الطريق نطلب من الله تعالى أن يوصله إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting إيانا would wrongly restrict guidance to us alone; unlike worship and reliance, guidance is not requested exclusively for the speaker's group.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن نقول إيانا اهدي بمعنى خصنا بالهداية ولا تهدي أحداً غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural اهدنا matches the prior plural worship and reliance, counters selfishness, and asks for others what one asks for oneself.
rows.anchor: فيه إشاعة لروح الجماعة وقتل لروح الأثرة والأنانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Traveling the path together brings strength and comfort; a solitary traveler may weaken, tire, fall, or be eaten by wolves.
rows.anchor: كلما كثر السالكون كان ادعى للاطمئنان والاستئناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communal salvation is a mercy, while punishment adds isolation to fire; the plural saved in 4:13 share company in Paradise, unlike the solitary punished in 4:14.
rows.anchor: في العذاب فيزيد على عذاب الكافر عذاب الوحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance request ties the chapter together: Rabb guides, Rahman and Rahim show mercy, worship and reliance require the path, and the favored oppose the astray.
rows.anchor: هذا الدعاء ارتبط بأول السورة وبوسطها وآخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat's fa'al pattern suggests encompassing breadth, unlike tariq or sabil; it is roomy enough for all travelers, as al-Zamakhshari describes it swallowing paths through its width.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري في كتابه الكشاف: الصراط من صرط كأنه يبتلع السبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite, construct, singular, straight path is one route to God's pleasure; other paths do not reach the goal, and scripture consistently uses sirat in the singular.
rows.anchor: مما يدل على انه صراط واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat is singular while sabil can be plural because the many paths lead into the one broad path; following other paths fragments people away from it.
rows.anchor: الصراط هو الأوسع وهو الذي تفضي إليه كل السبل

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi likens imam to a unique main highway and says Quranic imam can mean a community's law or a clear record/book.
rows.anchor: يقول الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي في كلمة الصراط وأخواتها

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi describes sirat as a unique passage between opposites, metaphorically monotheism and absolute divine justice, while other paths are relative.
rows.anchor: صراط: هو كل ممر بين نقطتين متناقضتين

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi describes sabil as a long, safe, easy but multiple route from one starting point to one destination; it can also mean rights, and ibn al-sabil is a legitimate stranded traveler.
rows.anchor: سبيل: الطريق الذي يأتي بعد الصراط وهو ممتد طويل آمن سهل لكنه متعدد

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi compares tariq to repeatedly traveled city streets and to regular acts of worship such as prayer, charity, fasting, pilgrimage, and remembrance.
rows.anchor: طريق يكون داخل المدينة وللطرق حقوق خاصة بها

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi defines nahj as a special route for particular groups and their distinctive devotional practices; he illustrates it with night worship and beneficence, with spending shared across the examples.
rows.anchor: نهج: وهو عبارة عن ممرات خاصة لا يمر بها إلا مجموعة خاصة من الناس

rows.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
rows.claim: Al-Kubaisi distinguishes a mountain pass (fajj), a heavily worn trail or track (jada/judad), and an underground passage (nafaq).
rows.anchor: فج: وهو الطريق بين جبلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing description covers all accountable people: the favored know and follow truth, the angered know but oppose it (some exegetes call them sinners), and the astray do not know it.
rows.anchor: ولا يخرج المكلفون عن هذه الأصناف الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past أنعمت identifies people whose favor has already been realized, including prophets and righteous predecessors, and links them across generations; 4:69 names them.
rows.anchor: ليتعين زمانه ليبين صراط الذين تحققت عليهم النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past أنعمت encompasses earlier and later generations who join the already favored; the present تنعم could suggest only a smaller group favored at one time.
rows.anchor: كان قوله سبحانه أنعمت عليهم أوسع وأشمل واعم من الذين تنعم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angered and astray are expressed as enduring states, while the verb for favor conveys renewal; this contrasts the lasting groups with an ongoing act of benefaction.
rows.anchor: الاسم يدل على الشمول ويشمل سائر الأزمنة من المغضوب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying أنعمت names God as giver, making the greatness of the gift clear; Quranic usage attributes good to God and often leaves evil's agent unstated or assigns it elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أراد سبحانه وتعالى أن يبين المنعم ليبين قدرة النعمة وعظيمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran attributes blessings to God, as in 28:17, 43:59, and 17:83; 33:37 uniquely says both God and the Prophet bestowed a particular favor.
rows.anchor: ولم ينسب سبحانه النعمة لغيره إلا في آية واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive المغضوب عليهم leaves the agent open so the condemned face anger from God, angels, people, and even their own skins.
rows.anchor: ليعم الغضب عليهم من الله والملائكة وكل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating لا ensures exclusion of either condemned group on its own; without it the wording might exclude only those who combine anger and error, as the two-part prohibition analogy shows.
rows.anchor: إذا حذفت (لا) يمكن أن يُفهم أن المباينة والابتعاد هو فقط للذين جمعوا الغضب والضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angered precede the astray because they know truth and reject it, are more culpable than the ignorant, and Jews preceded Christians; an authentic hadith identifies the groups accordingly.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح أن المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود وأما النصارى فهم الضالون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing defiance was the first sin in heaven with Iblis and the first on earth with Cain's murder of his brother; 4:93 also associates murder with God's anger.
rows.anchor: وصفة المغضوب عليهم هي أول معصية ظهرت في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angered oppose the favored just as anger opposes grace; the chapter's ending gathers its opening praise, judgment, exclusive worship, reliance, and guidance into the fates of the condemned.
rows.anchor: خاتمة سورة الفاتحة هي مناسبة لكل ما ورد في السورة من أولها إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha contains faith and good works, affirming God, the Last Day, angels, messengers, and scriptures, and joins lordship's unity to the unity of worship; it is therefore the Mother of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه السورة توحيد الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ما can refer to both the Creator and creation; the author leans toward the Creator, reading the oath as by the creator of male and female rather than by the created pair.
rows.anchor: الاحتمال هو مقصود لإرادة أن يحتمل التعبير المعنيين الخلق والخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes خلق as a verbal noun that can denote the created thing, unlike night and day, and cites زرع used both as planting and as crops.
rows.anchor: أحياناً يضع العرب المصدر موضع الذات

rows.speaker: السيد مصطفى ناصف
rows.claim: Mustafa Nasif argues that linguistic context is the primary fact and disambiguates a word's multiple possible meanings.
rows.anchor: يقول السيد مصطفى ناصف في السياق اللغوي أن السياق هو الحقيقة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that Arabic permits both definite and probabilistic sentences, illustrated by اشتريت قدح ماء and by the ambiguity of لا رجلا حاضرا.
rows.anchor: الجمل في اللغة على نوعين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence follows creation: night preceded day, the night and day preceded male and female, and the male preceded the female, as 4:1 indicates.
rows.anchor: فجاء ترتيب الآيات بنفس ترتيب الخلق: الليل أولاً ثم النهار ثم الذكر ثم الأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author asks why this verse omits الزوجين, unlike the parallel phrasing in 75:39 and 53:45; the segment ends before giving an answer.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال: (وما خلق الذكر والأنثى) بحذف الزوجين
